```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", width = 88)
library(readNBS)

series_coverage <- nbs_catalogue("en")
dataset_coverage <- nbs_dataset_catalogue("en")
```

`readNBS` provides a selected, versioned view of official National Bureau of
Statistics of China (NBS) data. It does not claim to mirror every NBS portal
series or publication. In package version `r packageVersion("readNBS")`, the
local metadata describes `r format(nrow(series_coverage), big.mark = ",")`
scalar-series identities across `r length(unique(series_coverage$family))`
subject families and `r nrow(dataset_coverage)` dimensional datasets. Those
dataset manifests enumerate 25,138 exact valid tuples in this version.

Coverage metadata is available without a network request. This article shows
the supported subject areas and historical starting points, then explains how
to inspect the exact identity or dimensional tuple used by an analysis.

## Read the coverage fields

For scalar series, `nbs_catalogue()` has one row per stable `series_id`.
For dimensional data, `nbs_dataset_catalogue()` has one row per `dataset_id`,
and `nbs_dataset_valid_tuples()` enumerates the combinations that the package
recognises as published. The central fields are:

* `available_from`: the earliest supported observation for that identity;
* `available_to`: the final supported observation when the route is bounded;
  `NA` means that the route is open-ended;
* `frequency`: annual (`A`), quarterly (`Q`), monthly (`M`), or ten-day
  (`10D`) reporting geometry; and
* `route`: the acquisition path, which distinguishes portal-backed series from
  retained release histories, press tables, and Yearbook snapshots.

An open-ended route supports requests without a fixed terminal date. It does
not mean that NBS has already published every future period, and it does not
guarantee that every period between the endpoints contains a non-missing
value. A finite end date identifies a bounded snapshot, archive, or
classification era. Always inspect the exact row rather than applying a
family-wide assumption.

## Scalar-series families

This table is generated from the installed scalar catalogue. “From” is the
oldest supported start among the identities in that family. “Open-ended” in
the “To” column means that at least one identity in the family has an
open-ended route; other identities in the same family can still be bounded.

```{r scalar-family-table, echo=FALSE}
family_labels <- c(
  capacity_utilisation = "Capacity utilisation",
  cpi = "Consumer prices (CPI)",
  employment = "Employment",
  energy = "Energy",
  fai = "Fixed-asset investment",
  gdp = "GDP",
  households = "Household income and consumption",
  industrial_enterprises = "Industrial enterprises",
  industrial_portal = "Industrial detailed portal series",
  industry = "Industrial value added",
  migrant_workers = "Migrant workers",
  output = "Industrial and energy output",
  pmi = "Purchasing managers' indexes (PMI)",
  population = "Population and demographics",
  ppi = "Producer prices (PPI)",
  ppirm = "Purchasing prices (PPIRM)",
  property = "Property development",
  retail = "Retail sales",
  services = "Services production",
  unemployment = "Surveyed unemployment"
)
frequency_labels <- c(A = "Annual", M = "Monthly", Q = "Quarterly")

family_coverage <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(names(family_labels), function(family) {
    rows <- series_coverage[series_coverage$family == family, , drop = FALSE]
    finite_to <- rows$available_to[!is.na(rows$available_to)]
    data.frame(
      Area = unname(family_labels[[family]]),
      Series = format(nrow(rows), big.mark = ","),
      Frequency = paste(
        unname(frequency_labels[sort(unique(rows$frequency))]),
        collapse = ", "
      ),
      From = as.character(min(as.Date(rows$available_from))),
      To = if (any(is.na(rows$available_to))) {
        "Open-ended"
      } else {
        as.character(max(as.Date(finite_to)))
      },
      check.names = FALSE,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  })
)

knitr::kable(family_coverage, align = c("l", "r", "l", "l", "l"))
```

The family counts include individual industrial, regional, product, and other
dimensional leaves that have scalar semantic IDs. Use a text search to narrow
the catalogue, then retain the coverage fields with the chosen identity:

```{r inspect-scalar-coverage}
population <- nbs_search("population", limit = 100L)
population_coverage <- population[
  , c(
    "series_id", "title", "frequency", "available_from", "available_to",
    "route"
  )
]
utils::head(population_coverage, 6L)
```

For a known family, inspect every supported identity directly:

```{r filter-scalar-family}
cpi_coverage <- nbs_catalogue("en")
cpi_coverage <- cpi_coverage[
  series_coverage$family == "cpi",
  c(
    "series_id", "title", "frequency", "available_from", "available_to",
    "route"
  )
]
nrow(cpi_coverage)
utils::head(cpi_coverage, 5L)
```

## Dimensional datasets and historical extensions

The 39 dimensional datasets cover exact published combinations rather than an
assumed Cartesian product. Their source paths include live portal panels,
retained press tables, longitudinal series, and six 2011 Yearbook bridges.
The following package-generated selection highlights the longest and most
useful historical paths; it is not a substitute for the complete catalogue.

```{r historical-dataset-table, echo=FALSE}
historical_ids <- c(
  "NBS/CN/A/DEMOGRAPHY/LONGITUDINAL",
  "NBS/CN/M/RETAIL_SALES/DETAIL",
  "NBS/CN/M/PROPERTY_DEVELOPMENT/NATIONAL",
  "NBS/CN/M/INDUSTRIAL_BENEFITS/BY_ENTERPRISE_TYPE",
  "NBS/CN/M/PPI/PRICE_DETAIL",
  "NBS/CN/Q/HOUSEHOLDS/INCOME_CONSUMPTION",
  "NBS/CN/A/MIGRANT_WORKERS/LONGITUDINAL",
  "NBS/CN/A/WAGES/LONGITUDINAL",
  "NBS/CN/A/INDUSTRIAL_CAPACITY_UTILISATION/NATIONAL_HISTORY",
  "NBS/CN/Q/INDUSTRIAL_CAPACITY_UTILISATION/NATIONAL_HEADLINE_2017_2019",
  "NBS/CN/10D/PRODUCTION_MARKET_PRICES",
  "NBS/CN/A/YEARBOOK_DEMOGRAPHY_LEGACY"
)
historical_rows <- dataset_coverage[
  match(historical_ids, dataset_coverage$dataset_id),
  c("title", "frequency", "available_from", "available_to", "route"),
  drop = FALSE
]
stopifnot(!anyNA(historical_rows$title))
names(historical_rows) <- c("Dataset", "Frequency", "From", "To", "Route")
historical_rows$From <- as.character(historical_rows$From)
historical_rows$To <- as.character(historical_rows$To)
historical_rows$To[is.na(historical_rows$To)] <- "Open-ended"
knitr::kable(historical_rows, align = c("l", "l", "l", "l", "l"))
```

The dates in `nbs_dataset_catalogue()` are dataset-level envelopes. Exact tuple
windows can differ: for example, the retail detail dataset has a 1990 envelope
because of its longest underlying history, while some of its leaves begin in
2000. Industrial-enterprise datasets likewise span several classification
eras with different starting points. Use tuple-level coverage for a final
selection.

Retrieve the complete dataset inventory with:

```{r inspect-dataset-coverage}
dataset_inventory <- nbs_dataset_catalogue("en")[
  , c(
    "dataset_id", "title", "frequency", "available_from", "available_to",
    "route"
  )
]
nrow(dataset_inventory)
utils::head(dataset_inventory, 6L)
```

Before selecting a panel, enumerate its exact valid tuples. This example is
local and deterministic:

```{r inspect-valid-tuples}
cpi_tuples <- nbs_dataset_valid_tuples("NBS/CN/M/CPI/PRICE_DETAIL")
nrow(cpi_tuples)
utils::head(cpi_tuples, 4L)
```

`nbs_resolve_dataset_series()` then validates one selected combination and
returns its stable scalar identity and source metadata. Unsupported Cartesian
combinations fail with a typed condition rather than silently selecting a
different series.

## Acquisition routes

Most scalar identities are portal-backed: 11,137 use
`portal_uuid_series`, while three retained official revision histories use
`press_revision_table`. Dimensional coverage combines the following declared
paths:

```{r dataset-route-table, echo=FALSE}
route_meaning <- c(
  portal_uuid_panel = "Portal-backed dimensional panel",
  portal_uuid_plus_press = "Portal panel with retained press coverage",
  portal_uuid_tree_plus_press = "Portal tree with retained press coverage",
  press_html_table = "Retained official HTML table",
  press_release_table = "Retained official release table",
  retained_longitudinal_series = "Retained longitudinal series",
  yearbook_snapshot = "Retained Yearbook snapshot"
)
route_counts <- table(dataset_coverage$route)
route_rows <- data.frame(
  Route = names(route_meaning),
  Datasets = as.integer(route_counts[names(route_meaning)]),
  Meaning = unname(route_meaning),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(route_rows, align = c("l", "r", "l"))
```

The exact row's `route`, `source_vintage`, `source_url`, and hash fields state
whether retrieval is live or retained and identify the source material used.

## Run the exact coverage audit

`nbs_historical_coverage()` joins the scalar manifest, all valid dimensional
tuples, schema eras, and required-history policies. It returns one row for each
scalar series or exact dataset tuple, with `available_from`, `available_to`,
`required_from`, `status`, `schema_era`, `policy_id`, and `authority` kept
together. The audit is entirely local but can take several minutes, so it is
best suited to release validation or an explicit analysis check:

```{r complete-coverage-audit, eval=FALSE}
coverage <- nbs_historical_coverage()
table(coverage$entity_type, coverage$status)

nbs_assert_historical_coverage()
```

The version 0.8.3 release audit contains 36,278 rows: 11,140 scalar identities
and 25,138 exact dataset tuples. All rows satisfy their declared historical
coverage policy; 1,268 have open-ended routes. A clean run took about 95
seconds on the release-validation machine, so documentation builds do not run
it automatically.

Use the family and dataset catalogues for quick interactive discovery. Use the
full audit when you need to establish that every supported identity satisfies
the package's historical-coverage policy.

## Scope and interpretation

Coverage dates describe the package's supported semantic and source paths;
they are not a statistical claim that concepts are comparable across all
years. Classification changes, release vintages, period geometry, suppression,
and missing observations remain explicit in returned columns. Longitudinal
datasets join eras only where the package has documented compatible concepts;
classification-specific datasets remain available when a single joined series
would be misleading.

Portal-backed routes retrieve current or revised official values and require
network availability. Retained histories and snapshots are deterministic local
paths whose finite coverage reflects their captured source material. The
package's MIT licence covers package code and prose, not NBS-derived data or
official publications; consult the source attribution and rights guidance
before redistribution.
